children: By Bharath Rajeswaran

Indian shares fell on Wednesday, tracking a global selloff after U.S.-Iran strikes heightened the risk of disruptions to oil flows, lifting crude prices, reviving inflation concerns and pushing global bond yields higher.
The Nifty 50
fell 0.89% to 23,841.40 and the BSE Sensex
shed 0.79% to 76,333.20 as of 9:46 a.m. IST.
All 16 major sectors slid. The broader small-caps
and mid-caps
lost 0.8% and 1.1%, respectively.
Brent crude

rose 1% to $95.4 a barrel, paring some gains after hitting a near-six-week-high earlier in the session, triggering a drop in Asian markets and lifting global bond yields on worries of a near-term U.S. rate hike.
Higher U.S. rates make emerging markets less attractive for global investors.
The U.S. said it had launched a series of airstrikes against targets in Iran overnight, prompting an Iranian response in a renewed escalation of tensions in the Middle East.

"Rising energy costs are stoking fears of sticky inflation, adding pressure to borrowing costs and weighing on richly valued equities, complicating the Fed's next policy move," said Devarsh Vakil, head of prime research at HDFC Securities.
India, a major crude importer, is particularly vulnerable to sustained oil-price gains because they can raise inflation and widen the import bill.
Oil marketing companies such as BPCL
, HPCL
and Indian Oil
, tyre makers such as MRF
, JK Tyre
, CEAT
, paint maker Asian Paints
and airline operator IndiGo
declined in trade on higher oil prices.
Bucking the trend, Coal India
gained 3.6% after the state-owned company said its total coal supplies increased 5.5% in August.
The company is selling a 10% stake in Mahanadi Coalfields (MHAN.NS) through the subsidiary's initial public offering, draft papers filed with the market regulator showed.
Sun Pharma
gained 0.5%, after becoming the sole Indian-headquartered company signing the most-favoured-nation (MFN) pricing agreement with the U.S., which removed the tariff overhang for two years.
